intro: High school teachers explain complex subjects and manage groups, skills prized in training roles. The closest of the 25 careers below teaches adult basic education and English as a second language, with a 92% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $61,540, which is 15% less than the $72,040 teachers earn.
why_it_works: A school day means planning lessons, keeping a room of teenagers engaged and adjusting when an explanation does not land. O*NET rates instructing at 4.12 out of 5 for this job and social perceptiveness at 3.88. College teaching, curriculum and corporate training use those strengths. Many better-paid matches need a graduate degree. The skills to build are operations analysis and managing budgets.
tips: Training and Development Specialists earn $69,280 with no extra degree and use your lesson design skills.
Instructional Coordinators earn $77,440, which is 7% more, but usually need a master's degree.
Keep your license active while you test a new role through summer or evening work.

faq.q: What jobs can former high school teachers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are adult education and ESL instructors (92%), postsecondary English teachers (81%) and Instructional Coordinators (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Training and Development Specialists are 79% matched and earn $69,280, which is 4% less than the $72,040 secondary teacher median.

faq.q: Which careers for secondary school teachers pay more?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more. Postsecondary political science teachers earn $98,070 (36% more), area, ethnic and cultural studies teachers $85,020 (18% more) and sociology teachers $84,290 (17% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All three usually need a graduate degree.

faq.q: Do secondary school teachers need another degree?
faq.a: Often. Only 7 of the 25 matches need no more education than high school teachers already have, and 18 usually need a graduate degree. A doctoral degree is the most common level in one close match, held by 58% of workers.

faq.q: What skills should high school teachers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, complex problem solving, managing financial resources and service orientation. Coordination already rates 3.75 out of 5 for secondary teachers in O*NET, so business and analysis skills are the main step outside schools.
